html:
Lavo was an early kingdom of central Thailand, centred on the city now called Lopburi, from about the 7th century to the 14th. The 500 map shows it early and stretches it far down the Malay Peninsula.

Lavo began as one of the Mon cities of the Dvaravati culture, which spread Theravada Buddhism along the Chao Phraya valley. From the 10th or 11th century it came under the Khmer Empire, and Khmer style temples such as Phra Prang Sam Yot were built there. Lavo also sent its own missions to China.

As the Khmer weakened, Lavo regained its freedom, and it later merged into the new Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya; see Sukhothai and Ayutthaya. On later maps it appears as the Lopburi Kingdom.
